capitals.name: Dresden
capitals.note: Dresden was Albert's seat as Duke of Saxony after 1485 (Partition of Leipzig page: Dresden as the centre of the Albertine Duchy of Saxony); it becomes the electoral capital when Maurice, the Albertine duke, takes the electorate in 1547 (infobox).

correction.text: the Ernestine electorate: Saxe-Wittenberg, the Ernestine Thuringian and Franconian lands and the Vogtland, without the Albertine duchy

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1486: the first year after the Partition of Leipzig (signed 'on 11 November 1485 in the city of Leipzig'). The electorate is the Ernestine share: 'The Ernestines retained the title of elector' (Electorate page) while Albert 'resided in Dresden as Duke of Saxony and was dominant in the east'; the Partition page gives Ernest 'the Electoral lands around Wittenberg' and 'most of the Thuringian regions in the west', Albert the old Margraviate of Meissen and domains in northern Thuringia; the Vogtland page has the Vogtland 'transferred to the House of Ernest' in 1485. The shape is the Cliopatria 1487 shape minus the Albertine duchy (the 1556 shape without Saxe-Wittenberg and without the Vogtland): 74 of 151 cells, about 18,700 km2, 49 percent of the Wettin lands. Cliopatria's House of Ascania row still draws all Wettin lands in 1486 (marked wrong there).

34,208 km2 for 1487-1491 in Cliopatria: all Wettin lands, Ernestine and Albertine. After the Partition of Leipzig (11 November 1485) the electorate is the Ernestine share only: 'The Ernestines retained the title of elector' while Albert 'resided in Dresden as Duke of Saxony' with 'Leipzig and Dresden' in his dominions (Electorate page). Corrected shape: the Cliopatria 1487 shape minus the Albertine duchy (the 1556 shape without Saxe-Wittenberg and without the Vogtland), 74 of 151 cells, about 18,700 km2. The Albertine half (79 cells, about 20,000 km2) is the state albertine-duchy-of-saxony until 1547. Precision of the proxy: Cliopatria cannot separate the lands around Torgau (Ernest's residence), of which about three cells fall on the Albertine side, and about six cells of Albertine ämters in northern Thuringia (Langensalza and others) fall on the Ernestine side. The Electorate page gives no area before 1805 (39,425 km2).

correction.text: the Ernestine electorate: Saxe-Wittenberg, the Ernestine Thuringian and Franconian lands and the Vogtland, without the Albertine duchy

keyframe_review.note: 34,252 km2 for 1492-1501 in Cliopatria (the 1487 shape, a re-cut of 0.1 percent): all Wettin lands. Corrected as in 1487 to the Ernestine electorate (74 of 151 cells); no page dates a border change in these years.

correction.text: the Ernestine electorate: Saxe-Wittenberg, the Ernestine Thuringian and Franconian lands and the Vogtland, without the Albertine duchy

keyframe_review.note: 34,026 km2 for 1502-1528 in Cliopatria (a re-cut under 1 percent): all Wettin lands. Corrected as in 1487 to the Ernestine electorate (72 of 150 cells); no page dates a border change (the Reformation under Frederick the Wise is not a border move).

correction.text: the Ernestine electorate: Saxe-Wittenberg, the Ernestine Thuringian and Franconian lands and the Vogtland, without the Albertine duchy

keyframe_review.note: 34,074 km2 for 1529-1546 in Cliopatria (a re-cut under 1 percent): all Wettin lands. Corrected as in 1487 to the Ernestine electorate (74 of 151 cells) until the Capitulation of Wittenberg (19 May 1547).

correction.text: the Ernestine electorate: Saxe-Wittenberg, the Ernestine Thuringian and Franconian lands and the Vogtland, without the Albertine duchy

the electorate after the Capitulation of Wittenberg: the Cliopatria 1556 shape (Saxe-Wittenberg and the Albertine duchy under Maurice) without the Ernestine Thuringian and Franconian lands and without the Vogtland

keyframe_review.note: 34,511 km2 for 1547-1551 in Cliopatria includes the Ernestine lands, which were not the electorate's after 19 May 1547: the Capitulation of Wittenberg gave Maurice, the Albertine duke, the electoral title and 'large parts of the Ernestine lands (including the core Duchy of Saxe-Wittenberg)'; the Electorate page: 'The Ernestines kept Weimar, Jena, Saalfeld, Weida, Gotha, Eisenach and Coburg.' Use Cliopatria's 1556 shape (25,005 km2), which drops those cells nine years late, and take the Vogtland out of it: the Ernestines lost the Vogtland tenure in 1547 and it came to the electorate by pledge only in 1559 (Vogtland page). The shape is the Ernestine electorate's Saxe-Wittenberg plus the absorbed Albertine duchy (merge event, May 1547).

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1556 shape without the Vogtland, valid from 1547

keyframe_review.note: 34,687 km2 for 1552-1555 in Cliopatria: same error. John Frederick I was released on 1 September 1552 but the electoral title stayed with Maurice; the Treaty of Naumburg (1554) settled 'several unresolved issues between the two Wettin branches' (terms not on the page). Use the 1556 shape without the Vogtland (pledged to the electorate in 1559).

25,005 km2 for 1556-1563 in Cliopatria: the electorate of Maurice's line with Wittenberg, 46 cells fewer than 1555; valid from 1547 (see the 1547 verdict). The Vogtland (6 cells at about 12.1E, 50.5N) is in this shape from 1556, but the Vogtland page has the Ernestines losing the tenure in 1547 and the Vogtland 'pawned ... to the Electorate of Saxony in 1559' (infobox annexation 1563): so this verdict covers 1556-1558 without the Vogtland. The Weissenfels page lists Langensalza, Weißensee, Eckartsberga and Sangerhausen as ämters of the electorate (given to a secundogeniture in 1656) and about six such Thuringian cells are missing from this shape; not corrected.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1556 shape without the Vogtland, valid 1556-1558 (the shape unchanged from 1559, see the next keyframe)
the Cliopatria 1556 shape, with the Vogtland pledged to the electorate in 1559

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1559-1563: Henry V and Henry VI of Plauen 'pawned the Vogtland to the Electorate of Saxony in 1559' (the infobox gives the annexation as 1563; in 1566 Augustus 'acquired the office and towns of Voigtsberg, Oelsnitz, Plauen and Pausa'). The Cliopatria 1556 shape already contains the Vogtland, so it is the right shape from 1559 (25,005 km2).

25,595 km2 for 1564-1578 in Cliopatria (+590 km2 over 1556): a re-cut, not an acquisition: three cells come in on the eastern edge (14.11-14.24E, 51.25-51.49N) and three scattered cells go out (11.31-14.21E, 50.9-51.74N). The Vogtland is not the change, since its six cells are already in the 1556 shape (it is pledged in 1559, annexed 1563 per the infobox, offices acquired 1566: Vogtland page). The Electorate page has 1567 only as the defeat of John Frederick II and Grumbach, which 'ended Ernestine claims to the electorate'. No page opened dates the re-cut.

25,660 km2 for 1579-1587: a Cliopatria re-cut of 0.3 percent (one cell out at 11.15E, 51.65N, one in at 10.91E, 51.63N); no page opened dates a change, and the Mansfeld sequestration is not on the pages read.

25,836 km2 for 1588-1618: +176 km2 over 1579 (four cells in between 10.91-12.76E and 50.9-51.63N, one out at 11.15E, 51.65N). The Henneberg share of 1583 lies south of that box (Schleusingen at 50.5N) and the Vogtland is already in the shape; no page opened dates the change.
26,011 km2 for 1619-1621. Lusatia was occupied in September 1620 and is not in the shape: it is drawn by the occupation events (1620-1636), not as Saxon land.
25,836 km2 for 1622-1625: the 1588 shape again.
25,572 km2 for 1626-1628: a Cliopatria re-cut of 1 percent; no page dates a change.
25,550 km2 for 1629-1631. Saxony joined Sweden in 1631 (Breitenfeld) without territorial change.

correction.text: the 1648 shape without Saxe-Weissenfels

correction.text: the electorate whole again: the Cliopatria 1763 shape

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1746-1762: the Saxe-Weissenfels line was extinct on 16 May 1746 and the duchy 'passed to the Electorate of Saxony'. The Cliopatria 1763 shape (33,373 km2) is used for 1746-1762. Against the 1648 shape (35,177 km2) it lacks 10 cells (11.15-14.44E, 51.65-52.2N: the northern exclaves, among them the Jüterbog cell, and one cell on the east of Lower Lusatia) and adds 5 (11.17-12.8E, 50.78-51.41N): 145 against 150 cells, about 1,800 km2 less. The Saxe-Weissenfels page dates one sale, 'sold Burg to Brandenburg in 1687', but the Burg exclave lies in no Cliopatria Saxony shape (0 cells), so it does not explain the difference; the 1746 gain no longer includes Burg. No page dates the other cells.

33,373 km2 for 1763-1790. The Treaty of Hubertusburg (15 February 1763) 'restored the prewar status quo', with no significant border change. Area check: the Electorate page's infobox gives 39,425 km2 for 1805 against 33,683 km2 here (ratio 0.85), within the factor of two; the shortfall is the seven cells missing against 1648, an unexplained Cliopatria loss.
33,395 km2 for 1791-1802: a Cliopatria re-cut under 0.1 percent; no page dates a change.
33,705 km2 for 1803-1804 (three cells more: Thuringia 2, Hesse 1). The Final Recess of 1803 gave Saxony nothing on the pages opened; the Electorate page lists no 1803 change. A Cliopatria re-cut.
33,683 km2 for 1805; infobox 39,425 km2 for 1805 (ratio 0.85).

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1805 shape held

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1806: Cliopatria's row ends in 1805; the electorate lasts to the elevation to a kingdom on 20 December 1806, and the 1805 shape holds.

ledger.note: 10 January 1356: the Golden Bull makes the Duke of Saxe-Wittenberg a Prince-Elector. The Golden Bull 'permanently granted the electoral privilege to the Duke of Saxony' (Rudolf I of Saxe-Wittenberg); infobox 'From the Golden Bull of 10 January 1356'. The land is the Ascanian Saxe-Wittenberg, 'centered at Wittenberg' (Cliopatria shape of 1363).

1423: the Ascanian line gives way to the Wettin. 'Albert III died in 1422 without male heirs', King Sigismund 'confiscated the duchy as a vacant imperial fiefdom' and in 1423 gave 'the duchy and electoral dignity to Margrave Frederick I of Meissen, a Wettin, because of his support in the Hussite Wars'. Same state, new dynasty.

region.text: the Wettin Margraviate of Meissen lands

ledger.note: 1423: the Margraviate of Meissen joins the electorate under Frederick I. The page gives the grant to the Margrave of Meissen; the land (Meissen, Dresden, Leipzig, Osterland, Pleissenland) is the Cliopatria 1556 shape without Wittenberg, a reading. The margraviate 'merges into the Saxon electorate' (Margraviate of Meissen dossier).

region.text: the Landgraviate of Thuringia and the Franconian part

ledger.counterpart: Landgraviate of Thuringia (Wettin line of Frederick IV)
ledger.note: 7 May 1440: Thuringia reverts to the electorate. Frederick II 'Landgrave of Thuringia, 7 May 1440 - 1445, succeeding Frederick IV'; Electorate page: 'Landgraviate of Thuringia reverted to the electorate' (1440). The region (Thuringia and the Franconian lands) is the cells Cliopatria drops in 1556, a reading.

ledger.counterpart: William III of Saxony (Landgraviate of Thuringia)
ledger.note: 1445: the Division of Altenburg gives Thuringia to William III. 'William III received the Thuringian and Frankish part'; 'Frederick got the Eastern part of the principality'; 'The mines remained common possessions.'

region.text: the divided lands of the Altenburg partition, chiefly Thuringia

ledger.counterpart: William III of Saxony (Landgraviate of Thuringia)
ledger.note: 1446: the Saxon Brother War begins between Frederick II and William III. 'led however in 1446 to the Saxon Brother War'. The page does not name the ground fought over; the divided Thuringian land is the reading.

region.text: the divided lands of the Altenburg partition

ledger.counterpart: William III of Saxony (Landgraviate of Thuringia)
ledger.note: 27 January 1451: the Saxon Brother War ends. The war 'found an end only on 27 January 1451 with the peace of Naumburg' (Frederick II page); the Electorate page calls it the Peace of Pforta, which 'confirmed the Altenburg partition'.

ledger.counterpart: William III of Saxony (Landgraviate of Thuringia)
ledger.note: 1482: Thuringia returns to the electorate. 'After Duke William III died in 1482, Thuringia returned to Frederick's line.' Region read as in 1440.

region.text: Albert's share of the Wettin lands: the old Margraviate of Meissen with Dresden and Leipzig (the Cliopatria 1556 electorate shape without Saxe-Wittenberg and without the Vogtland)

ledger.note: 11 November 1485: the Partition of Leipzig divides the Wettin lands, Albert taking the old Margraviate of Meissen (Dresden, Leipzig) as Duke of Saxony and Ernest keeping the electorate. The Partition page: the treaty 'was signed on 11 November 1485 in the city of Leipzig'; Albert received the Saxon ducal title and rule over the old Margraviate of Meissen, plus various domains in northern Thuringia, and made Dresden the centre of the Albertine Duchy of Saxony (1485-1547); Ernest 'necessarily received the Electoral lands around Wittenberg', 'acquired most of the Thuringian regions in the west' and kept several domains in southern Thuringia. The Electorate page: 'The Ernestines retained the title of elector' and 'Albert resided in Dresden as Duke of Saxony and was dominant in the east' (it dates the treaty of Leipzig 26 August 1485). The Vogtland page puts the Vogtland with the House of Ernest. Region: a proxy, the Cliopatria 1556 electorate shape without Saxe-Wittenberg and the Vogtland (79 of the 151 cells of the Wettin lands, about 20,000 km2); it puts about three cells around Torgau, Ernest's residence, on Albert's side and leaves about six cells of Albertine ämters in northern Thuringia on Ernest's side.
1547: the capital passes from Wittenberg to Dresden. Infobox: 'Wittenberg, 1356-1547; Dresden, 1547-1806'.

ledger.counterpart: Henry IV of Plauen (Burgraves of Plauen)
ledger.note: 1547: after the Battle of Mühlberg the Ernestines lose the tenure of the Vogtland, which Ferdinand I gives to Henry IV of Plauen with Maurice of Saxony as co-tenant (Vogtland page, which gives the year and no month). The Vogtland leaves the electorate until it is pledged to it in 1559.

19 May 1547: the Capitulation of Wittenberg gives the electoral title to Maurice of the Albertine line. John Frederick I was compelled to resign 'the offices and titles of Prince-Elector and Arch-Marshal'; Maurice became 'the first Saxon prince-elector from the Albertine line' and received Saxe-Wittenberg in 1548 (Electorate page). Same state, new line. The Albertine duchy joins the electorate with him (merge event below); the Ernestine electorate of 1486-1546 ends.

region.text: the Ernestine lands: Weimar, Jena, Saalfeld, Weida, Gotha, Eisenach and Coburg

ledger.note: 19 May 1547: the Ernestines keep their Thuringian and Franconian lands. 'The Ernestines kept Weimar, Jena, Saalfeld, Weida, Gotha, Eisenach and Coburg.' Cliopatria draws the loss in 1556 (the holy-roman-empire-minor-states dossier logs 46 cells coming to its row in 1556). The region is the cells Cliopatria drops in 1556, which also include about six cells of Albertine ämters in Thuringia (Langensalza and others). After 1485 these were the electorate's own lands (the Ernestine share); the Albertine duchy was a separate state.

region.text: Albert's share of the Wettin lands: the old Margraviate of Meissen with Dresden and Leipzig (the Cliopatria 1556 electorate shape without Saxe-Wittenberg and without the Vogtland)

ledger.note: 19 May 1547: Maurice, Duke of Saxony of the Albertine line, becomes elector and the Albertine duchy joins the electorate. The Capitulation page: the electoral title passed 'to the cadet Albertine branch, headed by duke Maurice', who 'became the first Saxon prince-elector from the Albertine line', with 'large parts of the Ernestine lands'; the Partition page: from then on the Albertine line in the former Meissen Margraviate ruled the Electorate (the page does not say the duchy was merged as a state; that is the dossier's reading, and the page's own dates end the Albertine duchy in 1547). Region as in 1485.

ledger.counterpart: Burgraves of Plauen (Henry V and Henry VI)
ledger.note: 1559: Henry V and Henry VI of Plauen 'pawned the Vogtland to the Electorate of Saxony in 1559' (a pledge; the infobox gives the annexation as 1563 and the text has Augustus 'acquired the office and towns of Voigtsberg, Oelsnitz, Plauen and Pausa' in 1566). The six cells are already inside Cliopatria's 1556 shape.

region.text: Upper and Lower Lusatia (the Cliopatria 1636 increment without the four Magdeburg towns)

ledger.note: September 1620: Saxon troops occupy Upper and Lower Lusatia for the emperor. 'Saxon forces occupied Upper and Lower Lusatia in September 1620 for the emperor. These lands were pledged to Saxony in 1623.' The Peace of Prague page has Saxony occupying them in 1623. Lusatia is a land of the Bohemian crown; the counterpart is the Habsburg monarch.

region.text: the towns of Jüterbog, Dahme and Burg, and Querfurt

ledger.note: 30 May 1635: the Peace of Prague gives Saxony four Magdeburg towns. The Saxe-Weissenfels page: Jüterbog, Dahme and Burg were 'adjudicated to Saxony by the 1635 Peace of Prague'. The Peace of Prague page (treaty 'dated 30 May 1635 [Old Style]') instead puts 'the towns of Jüterbog, Dahme and Burg Querfurt' under the Traditionsrezess annex of 1636. The Archbishopric of Magdeburg dossier dates Jüterbog's passing to Saxony in 1648 (from the Westphalia terms): disagreement. Reviewer eu-09-g: source moved from the Peace of Prague page, which dates the towns to 1636.
1636: Lusatia is Saxony's by cession. 'Under the Traditionsrezess annex of 1636, Ferdinand ceded both territories in perpetuity.'

region.text: Upper and Lower Lusatia (the Bohemian crown lands)

ledger.note: 1636: Ferdinand II cedes Lower and Upper Lusatia to Saxony in perpetuity. 'Under the Traditionsrezess annex of 1636, Ferdinand ceded both territories in perpetuity'; the Electorate page's infobox has Lusatia acquired at the Peace of Prague, 15 June 1635, and the lands 'pledged to Saxony in 1623'.
1642: Sweden overruns Saxony. 'In 1642, Sweden won a decisive victory at Breitenfeld, and overran Saxony.' Cliopatria's shrunken 1642-1647 shape is its drawing of this; the page names no cession.

region.text: Saxony, apart from Leipzig and Torgau

ledger.note: 6 September 1645: the Truce of Kötzschenbroda ends the Swedish occupation of Saxony except for Leipzig and Torgau. The German page dates the truce 27 August (Julian) / 6 September 1645 (Gregorian); the Swedish army may march through Saxony 'mit Ausnahme einer drei Meilen umfassenden Neutralen Zone um Dresden', Saxony pays 'monatliche Kontributionen von 11.000 Talern', and 'Die Städte Leipzig und Torgau bleiben schwedisch besetzt.' The Peace of Eilenburg (31 March 1646) cut the contributions to 8,000 talers until the general peace of 1648; the page adds that the country suffered under Swedish occupation until 1650. Reading: the country is no longer held, the two garrison cities are. This replaces the earlier confidence-1 bridge of October 1648 (the Peace of Westphalia).

6 September 1645: the Swedes keep Leipzig and Torgau under the Truce of Kötzschenbroda ('Die Städte Leipzig und Torgau bleiben schwedisch besetzt'). The Leipzig page opened for an earlier date says nothing of a Swedish capture or garrison, so the 1642 overrunning (Peace of Prague page) is the only earlier mark.

30 June 1650: the Swedes leave Leipzig after a tribute is paid. 'Swedish troops left Leipzig after a tribute was paid on 30 June 1650.' The pages give no evacuation date for Torgau; it is bridged to the Leipzig date (the German truce page: occupation 'until 1650').

region.text: the ämters of Freyburg, Sachsenburg, Sangerhausen, Eckartsberga, Weißensee and Langensalza, with the exclaves

ledger.note: 8 October 1656: Saxe-Weissenfels is cut off as a secundogeniture. John George I's will gave his younger sons parts of the electorate; Augustus received Weissenfels ('Death of elector Johann Georg I: 8 October 1656'). It later held Querfurt and the exclaves of Jüterbog, Dahme and Burg, and the County of Barby from 1659 (not Saxon land). Burg was sold to Brandenburg by Johann Adolf I in 1687 ('sold Burg to Brandenburg in 1687', Saxe-Weissenfels page).

union.text: Lower Lusatia west: Lübben, Doberlug, Finsterwalde

region.text: Merseburg, Delitzsch, Lützen, Bitterfeld and the Margraviate of Lower Lusatia

ledger.note: 22 April 1657: Saxe-Merseburg is cut off as a secundogeniture. Prince Christian received 'the castles, cities and districts of Merseburg', Delitzsch, Lützen, Bitterfeld 'and other former Bishopric of Merseburg lands' and 'the Margraviate of Lower Lusatia'; the 'friend-brotherly main treaty' was concluded at Dresden on 22 April 1657.

region.text: the districts of Zeitz, Naumburg and Haynsburg, with Schleusingen, Suhl and Kühndorf

ledger.note: 22 April 1657: Saxe-Zeitz is cut off as a secundogeniture. Prince Maurice 'received the districts of Zeitz, Naumburg and Haynsburg' (Schleusingen, Suhl and Kühndorf in 1660); a treaty of 1663 'delineated their territories and sovereign rights definitely'.

1706: the Swedes occupy Saxony. 'The Swedes occupied Saxony in 1706/07. The Treaty of Altranstädt forced him to give up the Polish crown temporarily.' Augustus II had 'won the free election for the kingship in 1697', and regained the crown in 1709.
1707: the Swedes leave Saxony. The page gives the occupation as '1706/07' and no month.
1718: Saxe-Zeitz falls back to the electorate. 'This line was the first of the three Saxon secundogenitures to die out in 1718'; 'Zeitz was merged into the Electorate of Saxony'.

union.text: Lower Lusatia west: Lübben, Doberlug, Finsterwalde

region.text: the former Saxe-Merseburg, with Lower Lusatia

ledger.note: 1738: Saxe-Merseburg falls back to the electorate. 'After the death of the last male heir of the Saxon branch line in 1738, the Duchy of Saxe-Merseburg fell back to the Electorate of Saxony.'

region.text: the former Saxe-Weissenfels, without the Burg exclave sold in 1687

ledger.note: 16 May 1746: Saxe-Weissenfels falls back to the electorate. 'Ducal line extinct: 16 May 1746'; the duchy 'passed to the Electorate of Saxony upon the extinction of the line'. The Burg exclave is left out: Johann Adolf I 'sold Burg to Brandenburg in 1687' (Saxe-Weissenfels page), so it did not fall back.

1756: Prussia attacks and takes Saxony. Frederick 'initiated the hostilities with his attack and capture of Saxony in 1756'; the Electorate page: 'The Seven Years' War began in 1756.' The page gives no month.

15 February 1763: the Treaty of Hubertusburg ends the Prussian hold. Signed 'on 15 February 1763 at Hubertusburg Castle' by Prussia, Austria and Saxony, it 'restored the prewar status quo'. Augustus III died in 1763 and the Polish-Saxon union ended (Electorate page: 'personal union ... 1697-1706 and 1709-1763').

1806: after Jena the French take Dresden. Saxony 'fought alongside Prussia at Jena. After defeat, Bavarian troops and a French commander occupied Dresden.' The page gives no month; Jena is of October 1806 from the wider record, not from the page.

11 December 1806: the Treaty of Poznań. 'On 11 December 1806, Saxony concluded the Treaty of Poznań with France. It then joined the Confederation of the Rhine.' The end of the occupation is the reading.

20 December 1806: the Electorate of Saxony becomes a kingdom. 'Frederick Augustus III became King Frederick Augustus I. The electorate was raised to a kingdom on 20 December 1806.' The Kingdom of Saxony has its own Cliopatria row from 1806.

wars.name: Saxon Brother War
belligerents: William III of Saxony (Landgraviate of Thuringia)

zones.text: the divided lands of the Altenburg partition, chiefly Thuringia

wars.outcome: The war between Frederick II and his brother William III ended on 27 January 1451 (Naumburg per the Frederick II page, Pforta per the Electorate page) and confirmed the Altenburg partition; William kept Thuringia to his death in 1482.
wars.note: The pages do not name the ground fought over.

wars.name: Capitulation of Wittenberg (Battle of Mühlberg)

zones.text: the Duchy of Saxe-Wittenberg, the core of the Ernestine electorate taken by Maurice (the Capitulation page: 'large parts of the Ernestine lands (including the core Duchy of Saxe-Wittenberg)')

wars.outcome: Maurice, the Albertine Duke of Saxony, defeated the Ernestine elector John Frederick I at Mühlberg, captured Wittenberg and took the electoral title by the Capitulation of Wittenberg (19 May 1547) together with large parts of the Ernestine lands; the Ernestines kept Weimar, Jena, Saalfeld, Weida, Gotha, Eisenach and Coburg.
wars.note: The page names neither the war nor its other battles; John Frederick was released on 1 September 1552. Corrected in the repair pass: the electorate of 1485-1547 is the Ernestine state under John Frederick I, and Maurice is the Albertine duke (Duchy of Saxony, 1485-1547), not the electorate.

wars.name: Thirty Years' War
wars.outcome: Saxony occupied Lusatia in 1620 for the emperor and received it in perpetuity in 1636; it joined Sweden in 1631 (Breitenfeld, Lützen), made peace at Prague in 1635 and was overrun by Sweden after Breitenfeld in 1642; the Peace of Westphalia was concluded on 23 October 1648 and the Swedes left Leipzig on 30 June 1650.
wars.note: The war article itself was not opened; the Peace of Prague page gives the 1636 annex and the 1642 overrunning. Second page: the German Truce of Kötzschenbroda page dates the truce 6 September 1645, with Leipzig and Torgau staying Swedish.

wars.name: Swedish occupation of Saxony and the Treaty of Altranstädt
wars.outcome: The Swedes occupied Saxony in 1706/07 and the Treaty of Altranstädt forced Augustus II to give up the Polish crown temporarily; he regained it in 1709. No land changed hands.
wars.note: The page does not name the war (the Great Northern War) or give months.

wars.name: Seven Years' War
wars.outcome: Frederick of Prussia attacked and captured Saxony in 1756; the Treaty of Hubertusburg (15 February 1763) 'restored the prewar status quo' with no significant border change, and Saxony's great-power status ended.

wars.name: Jena campaign and the Treaty of Poznań
wars.outcome: Saxony fought with Prussia at Jena, was occupied, concluded the Treaty of Poznań with France on 11 December 1806, joined the Confederation of the Rhine and became a kingdom on 20 December 1806.
wars.note: The page does not name the war.

certainty.note: The Wettin, Ascanian and Thuringian lands were lordships, pledges and divided inheritances; no treaty line of the electorate is dated on the pages opened.

The frontier with Bohemia is sharp from the Treaty of Eger (1459), which 'fixed the borders between Bohemia and Saxony' along the Ore Mountains crest and the middle of the Elbe. Every other frontier stays soft: the ämters in Thuringia, Lusatia and the Magdeburg exclaves are scattered, and the secundogeniture lands are drawn from circles around the towns the pages name.

sources.title: Electorate of Saxony
sources.note: Identity, the infobox (capitals, 39,425 km2 in 1805, Golden Bull 10 January 1356, kingdom 20 December 1806), the electors, the Wettin investiture 1423, the 1440-1485 partitions, 1547, Lusatia, the secundogenitures, Poland, Hubertusburg, 1806.

sources.title: Duchy of Saxe-Wittenberg
sources.note: Saxe-Wittenberg centered at Wittenberg, the Golden Bull of 1356, the extinction in 1422 and the 1423 grant; no area; the page is inconsistent on Frederick IV or I.

sources.title: Capitulation of Wittenberg

sources.title: Vogtland
sources.note: Repair pass: Vogtland occupied by Ernest in 1466, transferred to the House of Ernest in 1485, tenure lost by the Ernestines in 1547, pawned to the Electorate in 1559 (infobox 1563), offices acquired 1566, Saxe-Zeitz 1657, reversion 1718.

sources.title: Waffenstillstand von Kötzschenbroda (German Wikipedia)
sources.note: Repair pass: truce of 27 August (Julian) / 6 September 1645; Leipzig and Torgau stay Swedish-occupied; neutral zone around Dresden; Peace of Eilenburg 31 March 1646; occupation until 1650.

sources.title: Leipzig
sources.note: Repair pass: opened for the Swedish garrison; only the two Battles of Breitenfeld (1631, 1642) are mentioned; no capture, garrison or 1650 departure. Nothing used.

sources.title: Duchy of Saxony (1485-1547)
sources.note: Repair pass: returns the Electorate of Saxony text (no separate Albertine article, no area): Albert 'resided in [Dresden] as Duke of Saxony'; Ernest received the north, with his residence at Torgau; 1547 Maurice enfeoffed with the electoral privilege.

notes: Nine pages opened (the budget) and one failed: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Truce_of_K%C3%B6tzschenbroda (url_not_found, retried once); the repair pass read the German Wikipedia page of the truce instead (6 September 1645). CLIOPATRIA ROWS: the Electorate row is Saxe-Wittenberg (1363-1428, 5,458 km2) and then the Wettin electorate (1487-1805); for 1429-1486 the Wettin electorate is drawn in the House of Ascania row (see that dossier: 'the Wettin Electorate, not Ascanian land'), so this dossier carries new keyframes 1423-1486 and the Ascania shapes of those years should not be drawn twice. Cliopatria's 1640-1647 shapes drop Lusatia (1640) and the Dresden-Meissen swath (1642): marked wrong, since nothing on the pages cedes land (Sweden 'overran Saxony' in 1642). MODEL CHOICES: (1) the Wettin lands are one state until the Partition of Leipzig (11 November 1485), which is a split into the Ernestine electorate (this state) and the Albertine Duchy of Saxony (albertine-duchy-of-saxony, 1485-1547); Maurice's accession as elector in 1547 merges the Albertine duchy in and the Ernestine Thuringian and Franconian lands leave (Cliopatria draws that in 1556); see the REPAIR PASS below, which supersedes the earlier one-state reading; (2) the three secundogeniture duchies of 1656-57 (Saxe-Weissenfels to 1746, Saxe-Merseburg to 1738, Saxe-Zeitz to 1718) are separate states, subtracted from the electorate with circles around the towns the pages name; Cliopatria cuts only 12 cells in 1683; (3) Thuringia is out of the electorate 1445-1481 (William III) and before 1440 (Landgrave Frederick IV); the Thuringian and Franconian lands are read as the cells Cliopatria drops in 1556, which include about six cells of Albertine ämters (Langensalza and others) that the Weissenfels page lists as electoral land; (4) Lusatia is drawn as occupied 1620-1635 and Saxon from 1636. DISAGREEMENTS: Lusatia occupied September 1620 (Electorate page) or 1623 (Peace of Prague page; 'pledged' 1623 on the Electorate page); acquired 15 June 1635 (Electorate infobox), 30 May 1635 Old Style (Peace of Prague) or by the annex of 1636; Jüterbog to Saxony in 1635 (Prague and Weissenfels pages) or 1648 (the Archbishopric of Magdeburg dossier, from the Jüterbog page); the Peace of Pforta (Electorate page) or Naumburg (Frederick II page) on 27 January 1451; the Saxe-Wittenberg page calls the 1423 grantee Frederick IV of Meissen where the other pages say Frederick I; the Electorate page dates Leipzig 26 August 1485 (treaty) and 11 November 1485 (partition). NOT SETTLED: Vogtland, Henneberg, Mansfeld and the changes of 1564, 1579, 1588 (+590, +65, +176 km2), 1803 (+3 cells) are not dated on the pages; Burg sold to Brandenburg in 1687; the end of the 'pledge' of Lusatia in 1623; the Polish-Saxon union (1697-1706, 1709-1763) is a personal union, not territory, and is not drawn; the 1554 Treaty of Naumburg terms. Cliopatria's 1763 shape is seven cells smaller than the 1648 shape with no dated loss. Counterparts needing dossiers: saxe-weissenfels (1656-1746), saxe-merseburg (1657-1738), saxe-zeitz (1657-1718), the Ernestine Saxon duchies after 1547 (drawn in holy-roman-empire-minor-states), 'William III of Saxony (Landgraviate of Thuringia)' 1445-1482 and 'Landgraviate of Thuringia (Wettin line of Frederick IV)' to 1440 (Wettin lines, no slug). Gazetteer names this dossier lacks and drew with circles: Merseburg, Zeitz, Naumburg, Weißenfels, Sangerhausen, Querfurt, Jüterbog, Torgau, Lübben, Guben, and the regions Lusatia, Upper Lusatia, Lower Lusatia. REPAIR PASS 2026-10-25 (reviewer finding 1 and the four thin items). (a) Split: the Partition of Leipzig (11 November 1485, Partition of Leipzig page) is a split into the Ernestine electorate (this dossier: 72-74 of 151 cells, about 18,700 km2, in 1486-1546) and the Albertine Duchy of Saxony (albertine-duchy-of-saxony, 1485-1547; proxy region: the Cliopatria 1556 shape minus Saxe-Wittenberg minus a 25 km circle at Plauen for the Vogtland; 79 cells, about 20,000 km2). Keyframes 1482 (now to 1485), 1486 (new), 1487, 1492, 1502 and 1529 are corrected; the electorate merges the Albertine duchy in May 1547 with Maurice's accession; wars/1 belligerents are corrected. Proxy limits: the Cliopatria 1556 shape cannot separate the lands around Torgau (Ernest's residence; about 3 cells on the Albertine side) and about six cells of Albertine ämters in northern Thuringia (Langensalza and others, electoral ämters on the Weissenfels page) sit on the Ernestine side; the Partition page is silent on Torgau, the Vogtland and the Osterland. (b) Vogtland: the Vogtland page has it with the House of Ernest from 1485 (occupied by Ernest in 1466), the Ernestines losing the tenure in 1547 and the pledge to the electorate in 1559 (infobox annexation 1563, offices 1566): modelled as a 1547 loss and a 1559 gain, with a new keyframe 1559 and the 1556 shape ending 1558. NOT corrected: before 1466 the Vogtland is still inside the 1423-1465 shapes (the Meissen region of 1423 contains it) although the page has Ernest occupying it only in 1466 and the burgraves of Plauen holding it before. (c) Swedish occupation: the German truce page (6 September 1645) leaves only Leipzig and Torgau occupied, so the country-wide occupation now ends in September 1645 (it was a confidence-1 bridge for October 1648) and the garrison event runs from 1645 to 30 June 1650 for Leipzig and Torgau (Torgau's end is bridged to Leipzig's); the Leipzig page has nothing on a garrison. (d) The Cliopatria changes of 1564, 1579 and 1588 are re-cuts of a few cells (positions in the keyframe notes) that the Vogtland page does not explain; the Mansfeld and Henneberg changes stay undated. (e) The 1746-1805 shapes lack 10 cells and add 5 against 1648; the 1687 sale of Burg (Saxe-Weissenfels page) is not one of them (Burg lies in no Cliopatria Saxony shape); the 1746 gain of Saxe-Weissenfels no longer gives Burg back. (f) Disagreement: the reviewer proposes the Albertine share as the 1556 shape minus the 1363 shape; the Vogtland is also subtracted, since the Vogtland page is explicit that it went to the Ernestines. The URL for the Duchy of Saxony (1485-1547) returns the Electorate page's text (no separate article, no area). Five pages were opened beyond the nine of the first run (Partition of Leipzig, Vogtland, German truce page, Leipzig, Duchy of Saxony 1485-1547), over the page budget, because the finding and the thin items needed them. Counterpart needing a dossier: albertine-duchy-of-saxony (1485-1547).
